method: Read the jury brief, digest.md, brief.md, strategy.md (profile + Q1-Q6), fit.json, copycheck.json and looked at desktop-fold, mobile-fold, sheet-desktop, sheet-mobile and motion-sheet. Not verified: whether tapping a weekday actually changes the box compartments (the stills show a static small box beside the list), the text of the three collapsed FAQ answers (area, cuti/WFH, bayar), the pre-filled WhatsApp link target, and real-phone behaviour. Explain-back as the customer (office worker in Jaksel, on a phone before lunch) after the mobile fold: 'Dapur Seimbang antar makan siang lengkap, nasi merah atau shirataki plus lauk, sayur, buah, ke kantor di Jaksel Senin-Jumat, Rp 45.000 per porsi, minimal 5 hari, pesan lewat WhatsApp.' Passes: what, for whom, where, price, minimum and action are all on the first mobile screen.

reasons.business: The offer is complete and honest on the first screen (Rp 45.000, per porsi, langganan mulai 5 hari, Jaksel, Senin-Jumat) with the one action beside it (mobile-fold.png). The single WhatsApp action repeats six times with labels that grow more specific (Pesan 5 hari, Kirim pesan ini, Chat 0812-3456-7890), and the pre-filled message asks for exactly the four facts the kitchen needs, which cuts back-and-forth for a kitchen that answers by hand (sheet-desktop page-05). The price section turns the minimum into a week of five boxes = Rp 225.000 plus 'Tidak ada paket bulanan wajib', which is the risk-reducer from the canvas (sheet-mobile page-05). No invented proof, matching the brief. Held at 7 because the page has nothing that lowers first-order risk beyond the low minimum (no trial day, no named person, no kitchen) and the two biggest buying questions, delivery time and ongkir/area, are deferred to chat.
reasons.customer: Sections follow the customer's questions in order: what is in it, not a diet salad ('Bukan salad diet. Ini makan siang lengkap.'), will I get bored (week Mon-Fri), how much per week, how do I start, the leftovers in FAQ (sheet-mobile pages 02-07). Language is the customer's own (kantormu, nasi merah, shirataki, langganan, sekotak), sentences average 6.6 words, copycheck clean. Weak points against the profile's fears: 'late delivery' is the top fear and the first FAQ answers it with 'tergantung rute... kami kasih tahu jamnya' (sheet-desktop page-06), honest but no window at all; 'taste and fullness' is argued only by flat icon drawings in which the rice block is half the box and the lauk is a cartoon drumstick, which does not make anyone hungry (desktop-fold.png). 'Pilih salah satu waktu pesan' under Karbo is ambiguous: per order, per day or per subscription? (sheet-mobile page-02).
reasons.story: One device carries the page: the four-compartment box appears in the hero, labels the four parts, sits beside the week, and becomes the five small boxes that are the price unit (sheet-desktop pages 01-04, sheet-mobile page-05). That is a real through-line and ties the name Seimbang to the fixed four parts. But it is category-level, any bento caterer can show a divided box, and the strategy's own distinctive asset, a small kitchen whose owner talks to you on WhatsApp, is absent: no person, no kitchen, no voice beyond a neutral 'kami' (sheet-mobile page-08). The closing band 'Lima hari makan siang, satu chat.' is a good final line that restates the offer; the headline 'Makan siang seimbang ke kantormu.' is clear but not memorable.

problems: The page cannot answer 'jam berapa sampai' and 'ongkir/area' and so pushes the customer's top fear (late delivery) and a price doubt into the chat; the first FAQ answer is effectively 'ask us'. Fix is client content (a delivery window such as 11.30-12.30 and 'ongkir termasuk' or the list of kecamatan), then place it next to the price, not only in the FAQ. Screenshot: sheet-desktop.png page-06 / sheet-mobile.png page-07.

Appetite is not sold. The drawn box reads as an app icon: half of it is a maroon rice slab, the lauk is a cartoon drumstick, and on desktop the box is cropped at the right edge so sayur and buah are cut. For a customer who fears 'hambar / nggak kenyang', the dish names in the week list do more than the picture. Make the lauk compartment the hero of the drawing (named dish, e.g. ayam panggang bumbu kuning) and show the whole box. Screenshot: desktop-fold.png, mobile-fold.png.

No human behind the order. A first-time buyer is asked to send name and office address to a number with no name, no kitchen location, no 'dimasak pagi ini' fact; the strategy's own asset (small kitchen, owner answering by hand) is not used, so the story is generic and trust rests on the price alone. One line with the owner's first name and where the kitchen is (once the owner confirms) would do it. Screenshot: sheet-mobile.png page-06 (the three steps) and page-08 (closing).
keep: Price, minimum and area on the first mobile screen next to the WhatsApp button: lets a comparing customer decide in seconds whether to read on (mobile-fold.png).
Five small boxes = Rp 225.000 with '5 hari × Rp 45.000' and 'Tidak ada paket bulanan wajib': makes the minimum order feel like one normal work week instead of a package (sheet-mobile page-05).
The visible pre-filled WhatsApp message with four blanks: removes the 'what do I write' friction and tells the customer exactly what the kitchen needs (sheet-desktop page-05).
'Bukan salad diet. Ini makan siang lengkap.': answers the diet-caterer objection in the customer's words right where the box is explained (sheet-desktop page-02).

'Contoh menu satu minggu. Menu aslinya bisa berbeda.' and the footer 'Gambar di halaman ini ilustrasi, bukan foto menu.': honest labelling that keeps the page safe to launch before real menus and photos arrive.
